## Verdict

**Kelp** costs least for a team of 12, at **$96 per month**. It has both the lowest per-seat rate ($8) and the only minimum that falls below the team size, so the team pays for exactly the 12 seats it uses. Acme Desk and Fennel HQ both force payment for unused capacity — 13 and 38 wasted seats respectively.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Acme Desk | $14 | 25 |
| Fennel HQ | $19 | 50 |
| Kelp | $8 | 5 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 12 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Kelp:** minimum 5 < 12, so 12 seats paid. 12 × $8 = **$96 per month**. Effective rate $8.00 per person.
- **Acme Desk:** minimum 25 > 12, so 25 seats paid. 25 × $14 = **$350 per month**. Effective rate $29.17 per person ($350 ÷ 12), more than double the listed $14.
- **Fennel HQ:** minimum 50 > 12, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $19 = **$950 per month**. Effective rate $79.17 per person ($950 ÷ 12), over four times the listed $19.

Kelp is $254 per month cheaper than Acme Desk and $854 per month cheaper than Fennel HQ — $3,048 and $10,248 per year.

## Risks

Seat minimums, not per-seat rates, drive this result. But the ranking does not flip with growth: Kelp's $8 rate is the lowest on the list, so it stays cheapest at every headcount. Acme Desk's $350 is fixed until 25 seats and Fennel HQ's $950 until 50, so their per-person cost falls as the team scales — at 50 seats Kelp is $400 against Fennel HQ's $950, still well ahead.

Shrinking matters at the bottom end: below 5 people Kelp bills its 5-seat floor of $40.

This comparison covers list price only. The price list carries no information on features, support tiers, usage limits, or security posture, so a cheaper seat may buy a smaller product — nothing here establishes comparability. All figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual commitments, negotiated discounts, onboarding fees, and migration costs are not on the price list and could change the ranking.
